What else do you do before moving?","fact_ids":["sec04-F08","sec04-R02"]},"answer":{"text":"Glance over your right shoulder, toward the lane you are moving into.","fact_ids":["sec04-F08","sec04-R02"]},"rationale":{"text":"The blind spot cannot be seen from the seat even with mirrors, so the shoulder glance goes toward the new lane.","fact_ids":["sec04-R02","sec04-F07"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec04-u01-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Seeing ahead, curving and changing lanes","fact_ids":["sec04-F01","sec04-R01","sec04-F08"]},"lines":[{"text":"Scan far and wide.","fact_ids":["sec04-F01","sec04-R01","sec04-F08"]},{"text":"Handle curves in the right order.","fact_ids":["sec04-F01","sec04-R01","sec04-F08"]},{"text":"Clear the blind spot before moving.","fact_ids":["sec04-F01","sec04-R01","sec04-F08"]}],"narration":{"text":"This lesson covers three everyday skills that keep you out of trouble on any road. First, scanning: looking as far ahead as you can see so trouble never surprises you. Second, curves: when to slow, where to keep your car, and how to leave the bend. Third, changing lanes: the signal, the mirrors and the shoulder glance that clears a blind spot. These skills connect. Good scanning gives you time, good curve habits control your speed, and a complete lane-change check protects the drivers beside you. That is where you pick up pedestrians, hazards, vehicles that may cut into your path, and signs sending you a different way. Watch for clues that the driver in front may slow or stop: brake lights coming on, a turn signal blinking, or a cyclist or pedestrian on the road ahead. In the curve, look through it to where your path is heading, notice where oncoming vehicles sit in their lane, and keep your car right of the center line in the middle of your lane. Expect that a cyclist, a pedestrian or a slow vehicle may be hidden around the bend. As you leave the curve, speed up gradually rather than all at once. Slowing belongs at the start, steady control in the middle, and a gentle build of speed at the end.","fact_ids":["sec04-F04","sec04-F05","sec04-F06"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":44,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec04-u01-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"The reversed curve order","fact_ids":["sec04-R01","sec04-F04","sec04-F06"]},"lines":[{"text":"Wrong: hold speed in, brake on the way out.","fact_ids":["sec04-R01","sec04-F04","sec04-F06"]},{"text":"Right: slow first, build speed after.","fact_ids":["sec04-R01","sec04-F04","sec04-F06"]}],"narration":{"text":"A common trap is getting the curve order backwards. Some drivers carry their speed into the bend and only ease off once they see how sharp it is, then brake again as the road straightens. The rule runs the other way. Entering a curve, you slow down first. Leaving a curve, you build your speed back up gradually. It is never the reverse. When a question describes a driver braking in the middle of a curve or slowing on the way out, that is the wrong answer. The safe pattern is slow before the bend and a gradual, steady increase in speed as you come out of it.","fact_ids":["sec04-R01","sec04-F04","sec04-F06"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":43,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec04-u01-s5","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Blind spots and lane changes","fact_ids":["sec04-F07","sec04-F08","sec04-R02"]},"lines":[{"text":"A blind spot hides from your mirrors.","fact_ids":["sec04-F07","sec04-F08","sec04-R02"]},{"text":"Do not linger in others' blind spots.","fact_ids":["sec04-F07","sec04-F08","sec04-R02"]},{"text":"Signal, check mirrors, glance over your shoulder.","fact_ids":["sec04-F07","sec04-F08","sec04-R02"]}],"narration":{"text":"Every vehicle has a blind spot: an area around it that the driver cannot see from the seat, even using the mirrors. Because other drivers cannot see you there, avoid staying in someone else's blind spot. Now flip it around to your own lane changes. Before moving over, signal, then check your side and rearview mirrors for traffic coming from behind, then glance over your shoulder on the side you are moving toward. Mirrors alone never clear the move, because the blind spot is exactly the place mirrors miss. The shoulder glance is the step that covers it, so it is never optional when you change lanes.","fact_ids":["sec04-F07","sec04-F08","sec04-R02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":43,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec04-u01-s6","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Quick lane-change check","fact_ids":["sec04-F08","sec04-R02","sec04-F07"]},"lines":[{"text":"Both mirrors look empty.","fact_ids":["sec04-F08","sec04-R02","sec04-F07"]},{"text":"You want the right lane.","fact_ids":["sec04-F08","sec04-R02","sec04-F07"]},{"text":"What else do you do?","fact_ids":["sec04-F08","sec04-R02","sec04-F07"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: you want to move into the lane on your right, you have signaled, and both your side and rearview mirrors look empty. From behind the wheel, that zone stays hidden even when you use every mirror, so empty mirrors do not prove the lane is clear. The glance always goes toward the side you are moving to, not the other way, and it comes after the signal and the mirror checks.","fact_ids":["sec04-F08","sec04-R02","sec04-F07"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec04-u01-s7","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Scan, slow, glance","fact_ids":["sec04-F01","sec04-F02","sec04-F03","sec04-F04","sec04-F05","sec04-F06","sec04-F07","sec04-F08"]},"lines":[{"text":"Scan far and across the roadsides.","fact_ids":["sec04-F01","sec04-F02","sec04-F03","sec04-F04","sec04-F05","sec04-F06","sec04-F07","sec04-F08"]},{"text":"Slow in, build speed out.","fact_ids":["sec04-F01","sec04-F02","sec04-F03","sec04-F04","sec04-F05","sec04-F06","sec04-F07","sec04-F08"]},{"text":"Signal, mirrors, shoulder glance.","fact_ids":["sec04-F01","sec04-F02","sec04-F03","sec04-F04","sec04-F05","sec04-F06","sec04-F07","sec04-F08"]}],"narration":{"text":"To wrap up, keep three habits. Then you will learn where a pass may begin and end on a two-lane road, why the speed limit still applies the whole time, and the exact steps of a pass, including the mirror cue that tells you it is time to move back into your own lane safely.","fact_ids":["sec04-F09","sec04-F10","sec04-F11","sec04-F12"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":44,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec04-u02-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Room and timing","fact_ids":["sec04-F09","sec04-F10","sec04-R03"]},"lines":[{"text":"Do not tailgate before a pass.","fact_ids":["sec04-F09","sec04-F10","sec04-R03"]},{"text":"Know your car's acceleration.","fact_ids":["sec04-F09","sec04-F10","sec04-R03"]},{"text":"Early return risks a sideswipe.","fact_ids":["sec04-F09","sec04-F10","sec04-R03"]},{"text":"Late return risks a head-on crash.","fact_ids":["sec04-F09","sec04-F10","sec04-R03"]}],"narration":{"text":"A safe pass starts before you pull out. Hold back instead of tailgating, especially behind trucks and trailers, so you keep a good view of the road ahead, and know how quickly your own vehicle can accelerate. Then make sure there is enough room. If you cut back in too early, you risk sideswiping the vehicle you just passed. If you stay out too long, you risk a head-on crash with oncoming traffic. Those are the two ways a pass can fail at the end. And whenever you are not sure there is enough room, the answer is simple: stay in your lane and wait for a better chance.","fact_ids":["sec04-F09","sec04-F10","sec04-R03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":44,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec04-u02-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"The zone fixes both ends","fact_ids":["sec04-F11","sec04-R04"]},"lines":[{"text":"Two-lane road: pass on the left.","fact_ids":["sec04-F11","sec04-R04"]},{"text":"Start no sooner than the passing zone.","fact_ids":["sec04-F11","sec04-R04"]},{"text":"Finish before any no-passing zone.","fact_ids":["sec04-F11","sec04-R04"]}],"narration":{"text":"On a two-lane road you pass only on the left. The passing zone controls the pass at both ends. You may start no sooner than the point where the passing zone begins, and you must be finished before you reach any no-passing zone. Think of the zone as bookends. One end tells you the earliest point you may pull out, the other tells you the latest point by which you must be back in your lane. A question that has a driver starting early because the road looks clear, or finishing inside the no-passing area, is describing a pass that breaks the rule at one of those two ends.","fact_ids":["sec04-F11","sec04-R04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":44,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec04-u02-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"No speeding to pass","fact_ids":["sec04-F12","sec04-F10"]},"lines":[{"text":"Wrong: a short burst over the limit.","fact_ids":["sec04-F12","sec04-F10"]},{"text":"Right: the limit applies at all times.","fact_ids":["sec04-F12","sec04-F10"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap that catches many drivers. They believe a quick burst over the speed limit is acceptable as long as it finishes the pass sooner. It is not. You may not exceed the speed limit to pass, because going over the limit is illegal at all times, with no exception for passing. If the vehicle ahead is moving so close to the limit that you cannot get around it without speeding, then you simply do not pass. Answers that suggest speeding up past the limit briefly, or only when the road is clear, are wrong. The legal limit holds through every part of the pass, start to finish.","fact_ids":["sec04-F12","sec04-F10"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":44,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec04-u02-s5","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check the return risks","fact_ids":["sec04-R03","sec04-R05","sec04-F10"]},"lines":[{"text":"Too soon back in?","fact_ids":["sec04-R03","sec04-R05","sec04-F10"]},{"text":"Too long out?","fact_ids":["sec04-R03","sec04-R05","sec04-F10"]},{"text":"Name each risk.","fact_ids":["sec04-R03","sec04-R05","sec04-F10"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: why is it dangerous to stay out in the oncoming lane too long after you pass? So both ends of the return have a danger. The cue that keeps you between them is your rearview mirror. Once the vehicle you passed shows in it, you signal and move back. That timing is late enough to clear the passed vehicle and early enough to get out of the way of oncoming traffic.","fact_ids":["sec04-R03","sec04-R05","sec04-F10"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":44,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec04-u02-s6","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Steps of a clean pass","fact_ids":["sec04-F13","sec04-R05","sec04-F09","sec04-F11","sec04-F12"]},"lines":[{"text":"Clear path, mirrors, shoulder glance.","fact_ids":["sec04-F13","sec04-R05","sec04-F09","sec04-F11","sec04-F12"]},{"text":"Signal, speed up, finish quickly.","fact_ids":["sec04-F13","sec04-R05","sec04-F09","sec04-F11","sec04-F12"]},{"text":"Signal and return at the mirror cue.","fact_ids":["sec04-F13","sec04-R05","sec04-F09","sec04-F11","sec04-F12"]}],"narration":{"text":"To finish, put the steps in order. The other half is knowing where you must not. Signs and pavement markings show you where passing is allowed, and one rule sits above all the others: never pass where your view of oncoming traffic is limited. This lesson lists the specific places a pass is banned, from no-passing zones to hills, curves, intersections, railroad crossings and crosswalks. It finishes with the two narrow reasons you may still cross the center line inside a no-passing zone, and why neither of them ever turns into permission to pass the car in front of you.","fact_ids":["sec04-F14","sec04-F15","sec04-F19"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec04-u03-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"No-passing zones","fact_ids":["sec04-F15","sec04-F14"]},"lines":[{"text":"Do not cross the center line to pass there.","fact_ids":["sec04-F15","sec04-F14"]},{"text":"Do not start a pass you cannot finish first.","fact_ids":["sec04-F15","sec04-F14"]}],"narration":{"text":"A no-passing zone works in two directions. Inside the zone, you do not cross the center line to pass anyone. Before the zone, you do not begin a pass you cannot complete before reaching it. That second rule matters because a pass that starts legally can still end illegally if it runs into the zone. So as you approach a no-passing zone, judge whether you can be fully back in your lane before it starts. If not, stay where you are. Signs and pavement markings show where these zones are, and your own view of oncoming traffic is the final test even where a pass looks allowed.","fact_ids":["sec04-F15","sec04-F14"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":43,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec04-u03-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Hills, curves and crossings","fact_ids":["sec04-F16","sec04-F17"]},"lines":[{"text":"Hill or curve hides oncoming traffic: no pass.","fact_ids":["sec04-F16","sec04-F17"]},{"text":"Approaching an intersection: no pass.","fact_ids":["sec04-F16","sec04-F17"]},{"text":"At or inside a railroad crossing: no pass.","fact_ids":["sec04-F16","sec04-F17"]}],"narration":{"text":"Some places ban passing because of what you cannot see. When a hill or a curve blocks your view of oncoming traffic, you do not pass, because a vehicle could appear in your path with no warning. Other places ban passing because of what crosses the road. You do not pass when approaching an intersection, while at it, or while inside it. The same applies to a railroad crossing: not on the approach, not at it and not within it. Notice that the intersection and railroad bans cover the approach as well, so a pass that would carry you into either one is already off limits before you arrive.","fact_ids":["sec04-F16","sec04-F17"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":44,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec04-u03-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Crosswalk stops","fact_ids":["sec04-F18","sec04-R07"]},"lines":[{"text":"A vehicle stopped for a pedestrian: no pass.","fact_ids":["sec04-F18","sec04-R07"]},{"text":"Treated like the intersection ban.","fact_ids":["sec04-F18","sec04-R07"]}],"narration":{"text":"One more banned situation involves people on foot. If the vehicle ahead of you has stopped at a crosswalk to let a pedestrian cross, you must not pass it, on either side, for as long as it is stopped there for someone crossing. This ban sits alongside the ones for intersections and railroad crossings. Together they cover the spots where people or vehicles cross your path. When a question describes a car stopped at a crosswalk and asks whether you may go around it, on either side, the answer is no. You stop and wait as well, until the way ahead is clear.","fact_ids":["sec04-F18","sec04-R07"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec04-u03-s5","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Crossing is not passing","fact_ids":["sec04-F19","sec04-R06"]},"lines":[{"text":"Left turn: crossing allowed.","fact_ids":["sec04-F19","sec04-R06"]},{"text":"Blocked right side: crossing allowed.","fact_ids":["sec04-F19","sec04-R06"]},{"text":"Passing: never allowed in the zone.","fact_ids":["sec04-F19","sec04-R06"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap. In a no-passing zone you may still cross the center line in two situations: when the right side of the road is blocked, or when you are turning left. Some learners read that as a loophole, as if crossing for one reason lets them pass while they are over there. It does not. Those two reasons allow the crossing itself and nothing more.
